name: Pollux
description: A naked-eye star 10.4 parsecs away, 9.1 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Navy Precision Optical Interferometer.

radius.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 62509: radius 9.06 +/- 0.03 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 8.134 +/- 0.013 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax

mass.source: Hatzes et al. (2012), A&A 543, A98, abstract: M = 1.91 +/- 0.09 solar masses from the p-mode frequency spacing (7.14 +/- 0.12 microHz) and the interferometric radius

temperature.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 62509: effective temperature 4586 +/- 57 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit

radialVelocity.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331, XHIP, HIP 37826: RV 3.23 +/- 0.02 km/s (quality A)

distance.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 62509: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 96.54 +/- 0.27 mas, inverted

position.credit: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry

text.card: A naked-eye star 10 parsecs away whose disc the NPOI measured: 9.1 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 8.134 milliarcseconds, which gives 9.06 solar radii and 4,586 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 1, 4 and 5, HD 62509: parallax, limb-darkened diameter, radius, Teff
